description: One design element's embroidery parameters, as JSON values. Generated by `cargo xtask docs` from the parameter registry; the reference pages (params.md) describe the same parameters for people. Keys that are not listed are allowed: StitchCraft keeps them unchanged and reports them (SC-W0105).

angle.description: The direction of the rows, in degrees counter-clockwise from horizontal: 0 sews horizontal rows and 90 upright ones. A contour fill's rings follow its outline, and a meander fill's path its tile, and their angle turns only their underlay. A circular fill's angle turns its underlay and the lines its needle travels along under its spiral.
angle.title: Angle

auto_ignore_background.description: Whether the lowest shape is left out when it is the picture's background: an area under the other shapes that covers the whole design. A background is usually the fabric's own colour, and sewing it doubles the stitches and stiffens the design. What shows of it inside the picture sews still, as a white disc on a badge traced with its colours stacked does. Off, all of it that shows sews, as of any area.
auto_ignore_background.title: Leave out the background

auto_max_satin_width_mm.description: The widest a line or a part of an area sews as a satin column: satin stitches any longer lie loose. A line up to this wide is a satin column as wide as the line, and a wider one fills the area it paints. A part of an area no wider than this everywhere sews as satin columns between its outlines, and a part wider somewhere is filled, with its narrow parts sewn over the fill as lines and columns. As a traced picture's layers are flattened, an area wider than this somewhere is filled whole under the areas that fill its holes, and one no wider keeps its holes.
auto_max_satin_width_mm.title: Widest satin column

auto_min_area_mm2.description: The smallest area sewn. An area, or a part of one, smaller than this is a speck, which would sew a knot: it is merged into the area beside it that it shares the longest edge with, or left out when it shares none.
auto_min_area_mm2.title: Smallest area

auto_min_triple_run_width_mm.description: The narrowest running stitch sewn as a triple run, each stitch sewn 3 times (bean stitch 1). A line no wider than the design's narrowest satin stroke runs, and from this width it sews bolder than one stitch, which is as fine as the thread. A narrow part of an area is as wide as the circles that fit inside it along its centre line.
auto_min_triple_run_width_mm.title: Narrowest triple run

auto_overlap_mm.description: How far an area reaches under each shape sewn after it that it touches, and how far inside the edge of an area, or of a part sewn as a line or a column, that is sewn after it and covers it the area is cut away. The thread pulls stitches in from the edges of their shape, and without the overlap fabric shows between shapes that only meet. A satin column reaches as far past its rails, by its pull compensation.
auto_overlap_mm.title: Overlap

avoid_self_crossing.description: With inner to outer, the rings run the other way at every other level, so that the steps from one ring to the next don't cross. Off, only the middles run the other way.
avoid_self_crossing.title: Avoid self-crossing

anyOf.description: How many times to go back and forth over each stitch: 1 sews every stitch three times (there, back and there again), 2 five times. Several numbers separated by spaces are taken in turn along the stitches: "1 0" makes every other stitch bold.
anyOf.title: Bean stitch

anyOf.description: How many times to go back and forth over each stitch of the fill's path, before its repeats: 1 sews every stitch three times (there, back and there again), 2 five times. Several numbers separated by spaces are taken in turn along the stitches: "1 0" makes every other stitch bold. A circular fill's travel between the pieces of its spiral is sewn once, and takes its turn. A tartan fill sews its runs so, its rows and its travel once.
anyOf.title: Bean stitch

canvas_grid_origin.description: Lay the grid from the canvas's origin, so that cross stitch fills side by side share one grid and their crosses line up. Moved, the fill may then sew other crosses. Off, the grid starts at the top left corner of each part of the fill, which then sews the same wherever it lies.
canvas_grid_origin.title: Grid on the canvas

center_walk_underlay.description: Sew a running stitch along the middle of the column first, there and back. It holds the fabric still along the column, and suits narrow columns. The other underlays and the top stitches follow it.
center_walk_underlay.title: Centre walk underlay

center_walk_underlay_position.description: Where the centre walk runs, in percent of the way from the first rail to the second: 50 is the middle.
center_walk_underlay_position.title: Centre walk position

center_walk_underlay_repeats.description: How many times the centre walk is sewn: 2 goes there and back, 3 there, back and there again. An odd number ends at the column's end, and the rest of the column is then sewn from its end.
center_walk_underlay_repeats.title: Centre walk repeats

center_walk_underlay_stitch_length_mm.description: How long each stitch of the centre walk is. Between corners its stitches are spread evenly, so each one is at most this long.
center_walk_underlay_stitch_length_mm.title: Centre walk stitch length

center_walk_underlay_stitch_tolerance_mm.description: How far a centre walk stitch may stray from the middle of the column on a curve. A smaller tolerance follows curves more closely, with more and shorter stitches.
center_walk_underlay_stitch_tolerance_mm.title: Centre walk tolerance

clip.description: Keep the line inside the shape as drawn, before `expand_mm` grew it, where smoothing or the zigzag would take it out.
clip.title: Clip to the shape

clockwise.description: The rings run clockwise as the drawing shows them. Off, counter-clockwise.
clockwise.title: Clockwise

contour_strategy.description: How the path runs through the rings. Inner to outer steps in to the middle first and sews each ring round on the way back out. Single spiral turns in from the outline to the middle. Double spiral turns in, and back out between the turns it made.
contour_strategy.title: Strategy

contour_underlay.description: Sew a running stitch along each edge of the column, a little inside it, after any centre walk. It holds the edges still and keeps them crisp.
contour_underlay.title: Contour underlay

contour_underlay_inset_mm.description: How far inside each rail the contour runs, so that it does not show past the top stitches. It also stops short of the column's start by the first rail's value and of its end by the second's. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
contour_underlay_inset_mm.title: Contour inset

contour_underlay_inset_percent.description: More inset, in percent of the column's width at each point, added to the length above. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
contour_underlay_inset_percent.title: Contour inset (% of width)

contour_underlay_stitch_length_mm.description: How long each stitch of the contour is. Between corners its stitches are spread evenly, so each one is at most this long.
contour_underlay_stitch_length_mm.title: Contour stitch length

contour_underlay_stitch_tolerance_mm.description: How far a contour stitch may stray from its line on a curve. A smaller tolerance follows curves more closely, with more and shorter stitches.
contour_underlay_stitch_tolerance_mm.title: Contour tolerance

cross_offset_mm.description: How far the grid is moved: left by the first length, and down by the second. One length moves it as far each way. Moved by a whole cell, the grid lies where it was.
cross_offset_mm.title: Grid offset

cross_rotation.description: How far the grid is turned, clockwise for a positive angle. A letter turned along a path keeps its crosses square to it when its grid turns with it, from the letter's own corner (`canvas_grid_origin` off). On the canvas's grid, the grid turns about the point the offset names.
cross_rotation.title: Grid rotation

cross_stitch_method.description: The kind of cross. A simple cross sews its `\` diagonal and then its `/` diagonal over it, as the drawing shows it. An upright cross sews a `+`, its bar across and then its bar down, and a dense upright cross adds a second grid of them half a cell over. A double cross sews an upright cross between its 2 diagonals, and a Smyrna cross one over them. A half cross sews the `\` diagonal alone, joined into rows from cell to cell. Flipped, each cross is turned a quarter turn on its cell, so that a simple cross's `/` diagonal goes under, and a half cross sews the `/` diagonal.
cross_stitch_method.title: Cross

cross_thread_count.description: How many times the thread passes along each half of each bar of a cross. A full cross takes an even number, since the needle comes back to where it started: an odd number sews the even number below it, and 1 sews 2. A half cross sews each stitch an odd number of times: an even number sews the odd number above it, 4 sewing 5. More threads make bolder crosses, and pack the holes at the cells' corners.
cross_thread_count.title: Threads

enable_random_stitch_length.description: Vary the stitch lengths at random instead of spreading them evenly, or in a tatami fill, instead of placing the needle points on the stagger grid. Lines and rows sewn close together then do not line their needle holes up, which avoids moiré patterns.
enable_random_stitch_length.title: Random stitch length

end_at_nearest_point.description: End near where the next element starts: the column is sewn up to the end point, along the line under it to its end, and back, and ends on its edge nearest the next element.
end_at_nearest_point.title: End at nearest point

end_row_spacing_mm.description: The spacing of the last rows, for a fill that fades: from the first row the spacing changes steadily towards it, reaching it the part's height away, in each part of the fill. A circular fill's circles go from the row spacing at the middle to it at the part's farthest point. Empty, every row is the row spacing from the next.
end_row_spacing_mm.title: End row spacing

expand_mm.description: How far past the drawn edge the top rows reach: each part is grown by this much, with round corners, before its rows, rings or path are laid, or its cross stitch's cells are chosen. The thread's pull opens gaps between fills sewn side by side, and this closes them. Negative values pull the rows in from the edge.
expand_mm.title: Expand

exponent.description: How the lines are spaced. 1 spaces them evenly. Above 1 packs them together towards the first line, and below 1 towards the last.
exponent.title: Spacing exponent

fill.description: Whether the fill is sewn. Off, it sews nothing, and the shape's outline, if it has one, is sewn as its stroke settings say. The element before it still ends near it, as Ink/Stitch's does.
fill.title: Sew the fill

fill_coverage.description: How much of a cell, in percent, the fill must cover for the cell to sew a cross. Lower, crosses are sewn further past the fill's edges. At 100, only cells wholly inside it sew.
fill_coverage.title: Coverage

fill_method.description: The stitch the area is filled with. A tatami fill sews rows of running stitches across it, a contour fill rings that follow its outline inward, a meander fill one line that wanders through a tiling, a circular fill a spiral round its middle, a guided fill rows that follow a guide line, a linear gradient fill rows in the colours of its linear gradient, and a tartan fill a plaid of rows in the colours of its sett. A fill set to Ink/Stitch's legacy fill is sewn as a tatami fill without underlay (`SC-W0314`). A guided fill's strategies that offset its guide arrive in a later version, and until then an element set to one is skipped (`SC-W0011`).
fill_method.title: Fill method

fill_underlay.description: Sew underlay before the top rows, a contour fill's rings, a meander fill's path or a circular fill's spiral: rows of stitches farther apart than the top rows, square to them unless set otherwise. It holds the fabric still while the fill is sewn and lifts the top rows, so less fabric shows between them.
fill_underlay.title: Underlay

fill_underlay_angle.description: The direction of the underlay's rows, in degrees counter-clockwise from horizontal. Several angles separated by spaces sew a layer of underlay at each, one after another. Empty: square to the top rows, at the fill's angle plus 90°.
fill_underlay_angle.title: Underlay angle

fill_underlay_inset_mm.description: How far inside the fill's edge its underlay stops: each part is shrunk by this much, with round corners, before the underlay's rows are laid, so that none of the underlay shows beyond the top rows. Negative values let it reach past the edge.
fill_underlay_inset_mm.title: Underlay inset

fill_underlay_max_stitch_length_mm.description: How far apart the needle points along the underlay's rows are. Empty: the fill's longest stitch (`max_stitch_length_mm`).
fill_underlay_max_stitch_length_mm.title: Underlay longest stitch

fill_underlay_row_spacing_mm.description: How far apart the underlay's rows are, measured square to them. Empty: 3 times the row spacing.
fill_underlay_row_spacing_mm.title: Underlay row spacing

fill_underlay_skip_last.description: Leave out the needle point at the end of each underlay row, as `skip_last` does for the top rows.
fill_underlay_skip_last.title: Skip last underlay stitch

flip_copies.description: Sew every other line backwards, so that the ripple goes back and forth. Off, every line is sewn the same way, and the needle goes straight from each line's end to the next line's start.
flip_copies.title: Back and forth

flip_exponent.description: Pack the lines towards the other end: the spacing the exponent gives starts from the last line.
flip_exponent.title: Flip the spacing

force_lock_stitches.description: Lock the end of every group of stitches, and jump to the next, even where the needle would otherwise go straight on to it. The end lock is sewn even where `ties` leaves it out, manual stitch gets the locks it otherwise goes without, and a fill whose top rows `expand_mm` cuts into pieces locks each piece on its own.
force_lock_stitches.title: Always lock

gap_fill_rows.description: Rows sewn again where the fill leaves a stretch of more than 3 rows for another: that many rows past the stretch's last row, back and forth, before the needle travels on. The rows on the far side are sewn later, and the fabric between can be pulled apart by then; these close the gap. Rounded up to an even number, so the needle comes back to where the stretch ended.
gap_fill_rows.title: Gap-filling rows

grid_first.description: Sew the grid before the ripple's own lines, the whole ripple backwards.
grid_first.title: Grid first

grid_size_mm.description: How far apart the lines across the ripple's lines are: the ripple then sews a grid, its own lines and lines across them through every point they share. Empty or 0: no grid.
grid_size_mm.title: Grid size

guided_fill_angle.description: The direction the guide's copies move in, in degrees clockwise from horizontal as the drawing shows it. Empty, they move square to the line between the guide's ends. A direction near the guide's own brings the rows closer together than the row spacing, and the copies then reach only as far as the guide is long.
guided_fill_angle.title: Copy angle

guided_fill_strategy.description: How the rows follow the guide. Copy moves copies of the guide across the fill, a row spacing apart. Ink/Stitch's parallel offset and buffer arrive in a later version, and until then a fill set to one is skipped (`SC-W0011`).
guided_fill_strategy.title: Strategy

herringbone_width_mm.description: The width of the bands of a herringbone, each band's rows slanting at 45° to the stripes the other way from the band before, as the ribs of a herringbone twill turn. The weft's rows are joined from band to band along its stripes' edges. 0 sews straight rows.
herringbone_width_mm.title: Herringbone width

anyOf.description: How each line meets the next. Flat joins them with a straight run of stitches. Point bends each line into the next, so that they meet at a point, and the ripple has 1 line more to bend.
anyOf.title: Join style

anyOf.description: How the rings turn at the shape's corners, as they move in a row spacing at a time: round, mitred (pointed, cut off 10 row spacings out) or bevelled (cut straight across).
anyOf.title: Join style

line_count.description: How many lines the ripple sews. The first is the stroke's own line, or a column's first rail, and the last the target point, or the second rail. Along a guide, how many copies of the line it places. With `min_line_dist_mm`, this keeps only the count's parity, odd or even.
line_count.title: Lines

lock_custom_end.description: The steps a custom end lock takes along the stitching after it ends, as numbers separated by spaces, each a number of `lock_end_scale_mm`. Positive steps go back into the stitching. The first step starts where the stitching ends, and `1 -1 1 -1` goes back and forth twice. Or an SVG path that draws the lock in millimetres, at `lock_end_scale_percent`, as a start lock's path draws it. Its last segment points along the last stitch, back into the stitching, and is not sewn. The lock is sewn backwards, from where the stitching ends, which is where that segment starts, through the nodes before it to the path's first node. A path that cannot be sewn as written is named (`SC-W0503`).
lock_custom_end.title: Custom end lock

lock_custom_start.description: The steps a custom start lock takes along the stitching before it starts, as numbers separated by spaces, each a number of `lock_start_scale_mm`. Positive steps go into the stitching. The last step ends where the stitching starts, and `1 -1 1 -1` goes forth and back twice. Or an SVG path that draws the lock in millimetres, at `lock_start_scale_percent`. Its last segment points along the first stitch, into the stitching, and is not sewn. It starts where the stitching starts, and the nodes before it are sewn first, in order. `M 0,0 L 0,1 L 1,1 L 1,0 L 2,0` sews 3 sides of a square 1 mm across behind the start. A path that cannot be sewn as written is named (`SC-W0503`).
lock_custom_start.title: Custom start lock

lock_end.description: The shape of the lock stitches at the end. The half stitch goes back and forth over the last half of the last stitch, which hides it. The other shapes are larger and grip more.
lock_end.title: End lock

lock_end_scale_mm.description: How long each step of an end lock made of steps (back and forth, or custom numbers) is.
lock_end_scale_mm.title: End lock size

lock_end_scale_percent.description: How large a drawn end lock is, in percent of its own size: at 100 % it reaches about 1.4 mm along the stitching. A custom path is drawn in millimetres at 100 %.
lock_end_scale_percent.title: End lock scale

lock_start.description: The shape of the lock stitches at the start. The half stitch goes back and forth over the first half of the first stitch, which hides it. The other shapes are larger and grip more.
lock_start.title: Start lock

lock_start_scale_mm.description: How long each step of a start lock made of steps (back and forth, or custom numbers) is.
lock_start_scale_mm.title: Start lock size

lock_start_scale_percent.description: How large a drawn start lock is, in percent of its own size: at 100 % it reaches about 1.4 mm along the stitching. A custom path is drawn in millimetres at 100 %.
lock_start_scale_percent.title: Start lock scale

manual_pattern_placement.description: Sew each line through the points it is made of, and nothing between them: the stroke's nodes, copied, where a line is copied, and the stitch length is not used along the lines. A straight run of stitches no longer than the stitch length joins each line to the next.
manual_pattern_placement.title: Sew the line's own nodes

max_cross_stitch_length_mm.description: The longest stitch a cross sews. A diagonal longer than this, on a large grid, is sewn in equal stitches, each no longer. Half crosses travel between their rows in stitches this long.
max_cross_stitch_length_mm.title: Longest cross stitch

max_stitch_length_mm.description: Manual stitch splits a stitch longer than this into equal parts, and a satin column splits it as its split method says. Empty, a stitch is split only where it is longer than the machine sews. A tatami fill sews its rows in stitches this long, and a contour fill its rings. A meander or circular fill's underlay sews its rows so, and a tartan fill its rows and its weft's runs.
max_stitch_length_mm.title: Longest stitch

meander_angle.description: How far the tiling is turned, in degrees clockwise as the drawing shows it.
meander_angle.title: Pattern angle

meander_pattern.description: The tiling whose sides the line wanders along: hexagons, squares, triangles, or 2 or 3 kinds of polygon. Its sides are 2 mm long at a scale of 100 %. A fill set to one of Ink/Stitch's tiles, which StitchCraft doesn't have, wanders through the honeycomb (`SC-W0316`).
meander_pattern.title: Pattern

meander_scale_percent.description: How large the tiling is, in percent: 100 makes its sides 2 mm long. 2 percentages separated by a space scale it across and down apart. Each is at least 1.
meander_scale_percent.title: Pattern scale

min_jump_stitch_length_mm.description: A move to the next element no longer than this is sewn straight on, without lock stitches or a jump. Empty: the document's setting.
min_jump_stitch_length_mm.title: Shortest jump

min_line_dist_mm.description: How far apart the lines are at least. The count is then the shortest distance from the stroke's line to the target point, or across the column, or the guide's length, divided by this and rounded up. Where that differs in parity from `line_count`, it is 1 less, so that the ripple ends on the same side however large it is drawn. Empty or 0: `line_count` gives the count.
min_line_dist_mm.title: Least distance between lines

min_random_split_length_mm.description: With a random split phase, also split stitches longer than this but no longer than the longest stitch. 0 splits every stitch. Empty: the longest stitch.
min_random_split_length_mm.title: Shortest split stitch

min_stitch_length_mm.description: Stitches shorter than this are merged into their neighbours, so the needle does not hammer one hole. Empty: the larger of the document's setting and the machine's minimum.
min_stitch_length_mm.title: Shortest stitch

pattern_size_mm.description: How wide and how tall the grid's cells are, each the size of a cross. One length gives square cells, and 2 separated by a space give the width, then the height.
pattern_size_mm.title: Cell size

pull_compensation_mm.description: How far each end of every stitch reaches past the shape's edge: a satin column's stitches past its rails, and a fill's rows past its outline and its holes. The thread pulls the fabric in along the stitches as it sews, so a shape comes out smaller than drawn, and this makes up for it. 2 values set the 2 ends: a satin's first rail's side, then the second's, or the end each fill row starts from at the fill's angle, then the other (at 0°, the left end, then the right). Negative values make a satin narrower; a fill reads them as 0, as Ink/Stitch does.
pull_compensation_mm.title: Pull compensation

pull_compensation_percent.description: More pull compensation, in percent of each stitch's length, added to the length above: a satin's stitches reach out by a share of the column's width there, and a fill's rows by a share of each row's length, so wide parts and long rows reach further. 2 values set the 2 ends, as above. A fill reads negative values as 0, as Ink/Stitch does.
pull_compensation_percent.title: Pull compensation (%)

push_compensation_mm.description: How much shorter the column is made at its start and its end. Satin stitches push the fabric out along the column, so it comes out longer than drawn, and this makes up for it. Negative values lengthen the column. 2 values set the start, then the end.
push_compensation_mm.title: Push compensation

random_seed.description: Where random variation starts: a running stitch's random lengths, a satin column's random widths and spacing, and a tatami or contour fill's random lengths. The same seed gives the same stitches, another seed others, and elements alike given one seed vary alike. Empty, each element gets its own.
random_seed.title: Random seed

random_split_jitter_percent.description: How far each split may move at random, in percent of a part, either way. With a random split phase, how much each part's length may vary instead.
random_split_jitter_percent.title: Split jitter

random_split_phase.description: Start each stitch's splits at a random distance from its start, and space them by the longest stitch, instead of dividing the stitch evenly. The needle holes of neighbouring stitches then fall apart, at the cost of a few more stitches.
random_split_phase.title: Random split phase

random_stitch_length_jitter_percent.description: How much each stitch may be longer or shorter than the stitch length, in percent of it. A tatami or contour fill's stitch length is its longest stitch. Where the random lengths start is the element's `random_seed`.
random_stitch_length_jitter_percent.title: Length variation

random_width_decrease_percent.description: How much narrower than the compensated column a stitch may come out on each side, chosen at random for each stitch, in percent of the column's width there. A ragged edge looks like fur or grass. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
random_width_decrease_percent.title: Random width decrease

random_width_increase_percent.description: How much wider than the compensated column a stitch may come out on each side, chosen at random for each stitch, in percent of the column's width there. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
random_width_increase_percent.title: Random width increase

random_zigzag_spacing_percent.description: How much the distance to each stitch may differ from the zigzag spacing, chosen at random, in percent of the spacing, longer or shorter.
random_zigzag_spacing_percent.title: Random zigzag spacing

anyOf.description: How many times to sew along the path: 2 goes there and back, 3 there, back and there again. An even number ends where the path starts, which suits a line that must come back.
anyOf.title: Repeats

anyOf.description: How often to sew the fill's path. Each repeat after the first sews everything sewn so far again, the other way round, so the passes double: 1 sews it once, 2 there and back, 3 there and back twice, 4 there and back 4 times.
anyOf.title: Repeats

reverse.description: Sew the whole ripple the other way round, from its last needle point to its first.
reverse.title: Reverse

anyOf.description: Which rails of the column the ripple runs along, or of its satin guide, are read against the way they are drawn, so that both run the same way. Automatic reverses the second rail when it runs against the first.
anyOf.title: Reverse rails

anyOf.description: Which rails are sewn against the way they are drawn, so that both run the same way. Automatic reverses the second rail when it runs against the first.
anyOf.title: Reverse rails

rotate_ripples.description: Turn each copy as the guide turns: by the angle from the guide's start to the way it runs there, or for a closed line on a satin guide, as the rails' pairs turn from the first.
rotate_ripples.title: Turn with the guide

row_spacing_mm.description: How far apart the rows are, measured square to them, or a contour fill's rings, or a circular fill's circles. Rows closer together cover the fabric more fully, and pull it in more. A meander fill's underlay rows lie 3 of them apart.
row_spacing_mm.title: Row spacing

rows_per_thread.description: How many rows in a row go to the warp's stripes, before as many go to the weft's. More rows to a thread make the weave coarser, as a heavier twill.
rows_per_thread.title: Rows per thread

running_stitch_length_mm.description: How long each stitch is. Between corners the stitches are spread evenly, so each one is at most this long. Several lengths separated by spaces sew as a repeating pattern: "2.5 1" sews long, short, long, short. The stitches that join a satin column's underlays are no longer than the first length, and a meander fill's path and a circular fill's spiral are sewn in stitches of the first length.
running_stitch_length_mm.title: Stitch length

running_stitch_position.description: Where the line the needle follows to the start and to the end runs, in percent of the way from the first rail to the second: 50 is the middle.
running_stitch_position.title: Running stitch position

running_stitch_tolerance_mm.description: How far a stitch may stray from a curve. A smaller tolerance follows curves more closely, with more and shorter stitches. A satin column's way to its start and from its end keeps to it too, as do a contour fill's rings.
running_stitch_tolerance_mm.title: Curve tolerance

satin_column.description: Sew the path as a satin column. Two of its subpaths are the rails, the column's edges, and the others are rungs across both, which say which point of one rail goes with which of the other. Without rungs, the rails' nodes pair up instead. A path of 1 subpath is the column's centre line: the column is as wide as the stroke, and turns its corners as the stroke's join does. Off, the path is sewn as a stroke, by its `stroke_method`.
satin_column.title: Satin column

satin_guide_pattern_position.description: Where the copies lie along a guide. Line count places them as `line_count` or `min_line_dist_mm` says, spread along the guide. At the rungs places one at each point of a guide line, or at each rung of a satin guide. Adaptive places one wherever it clears the last by `min_line_dist_mm` between a satin guide's rails.
satin_guide_pattern_position.title: Copies along the guide

satin_method.description: How the column is sewn. A satin column sews stitches straight across it, from one rail to the other and back. An E-stitch sews a spike across the column at each pair and a spine along its first rail between them, an edge for appliqué. An S-stitch sews one stitch across at each pair, every other one the other way, with a step along a rail between them: split by a longest stitch, they cover the column in rows, as a fill does. A zigzag satin sews a zigzag between the rails, every stitch slanting half the spacing along.
satin_method.title: Method

scale_axis.description: Which way the copies are scaled along a guide line, and along a satin guide for a closed line: both ways, across (x), down (y), or neither.
scale_axis.title: Scale axis

scale_end.description: How large the last copy along a guide line is, in percent of the line. The copies between grow or shrink evenly from the first's size to this.
scale_end.title: Last copy's size

scale_start.description: How large the first copy along a guide line is, in percent of the line.
scale_start.title: First copy's size

short_stitch_distance_mm.description: How close a needle point may come to the last one left in place on its rail before it is moved in. 0 moves none.
short_stitch_distance_mm.title: Short stitch distance

short_stitch_inset.description: How far a crowded needle point is moved in along its stitch, in percent of the stitch's width. On the inside of a tight curve the needle points of a rail crowd together, and the thread piles up there. Moving some of them in spreads them out. Points that crowd one after another take turns with several values separated by spaces.
short_stitch_inset.title: Short stitch inset

skip_end.description: How many of the last lines are left out, such as the lines that crowd round the target point.
skip_end.title: Skip last lines

skip_last.description: Leave out the needle point at the end of each row, or of each piece of a circular fill's spiral. It lies close to the start of the next, and leaving it out lowers the stitch count and the density along the fill's edge.
skip_last.title: Skip last stitch

skip_start.description: How many of the first lines are left out, such as the stroke's own line.
skip_start.title: Skip first lines

smoothness_mm.description: How much the path is smoothed: its corners are cut round over about 5 times this. A contour fill sewn inner to outer is then kept inside the fill, and a meander fill with `clip` on. 0 leaves the path as it is. A contour fill's spirals are not smoothed.
smoothness_mm.title: Smoothness

split_method.description: How stitches longer than the longest stitch (`max_stitch_length_mm`) are split. Default splits each into the fewest equal parts no longer than it. Simple splits at whole multiples of it from the stitch's start. Staggered moves those splits along from one stitch to the next, so the needle holes of neighbouring stitches do not line up in a row.
split_method.title: Split method

split_staggers.description: How many stitches the staggered splits take to come back to where they started. A fraction draws diagonals that show less than whole numbers do.
split_staggers.title: Staggers

anyOf.description: How many lines the needle points take to come back to where they started. Each line's needle points start a staggers-th of the stitch lengths further back than the line's before, so that lines side by side don't line them up. 0 places every line's needle points from the end it is sewn from.
anyOf.title: Staggers

anyOf.description: How many rows the needle points take to come back to where they started. Along each row they lie the longest stitch (`max_stitch_length_mm`) apart, a `staggers`-th of a stitch along from the row before's, so that neighbouring rows never line them up. A fraction draws diagonals that show less than whole numbers do. A negative number staggers the rows the other way, and 0 counts as 1, which lines every row's points up, as in Ink/Stitch. A contour or meander fill staggers its underlay's rows so.
anyOf.title: Staggers

start_at_nearest_point.description: Start near where the elements before left the needle: on the line between the rails, or on the column's edge when only that is close, then along the line under the column to its start. It saves a jump and a trim.
start_at_nearest_point.title: Start at nearest point

stitch_position_method.description: Where the needle points lie along each row. Flexible spreads a row's stitches evenly between its corners. Flexible (stagger) sews whole stitches of the longest stitch from where the row's stagger starts it, round its corners, and the last one shorter, so that the rows' needle points keep their stagger.
stitch_position_method.title: Stitch positions

stop_after.description: Pause the machine after this element: to add an appliqué fabric, or to check the work.
stop_after.title: Stop after

stop_at_ending_point.description: End the fill's colours at its end position, or near the next element. A tartan fill's every colour then travels from where the fill starts to where it ends, and a linear gradient fill's last 2 colours travel on to the end after their rows. Off, each colour ends with its last row, and a tartan starts each colour where the one before ended, and only its runs travel on towards its end.
stop_at_ending_point.title: Stop at the end position

stroke_method.description: The stitch the path is sewn with. A running stitch goes along it and a zigzag across it, and manual stitch puts a needle point on each of its nodes. A ripple stitch sews lines that spread out from the path to its target point, or along it from one rail to the other where it is drawn as a satin column's rails and rungs.
stroke_method.title: Method

stroke_pull_compensation_mm.description: How much further out than half the stroke's width the needle goes on each side, to make up for the thread pulling the fabric in. 2 values set the 2 sides: the left of the way the path goes, then the right. Negative values make the zigzag narrower.
stroke_pull_compensation_mm.title: Pull compensation

anyOf.description: Make the second rail of the column, or of the satin guide, the first: the ripple starts on it.
anyOf.title: Swap rails

anyOf.description: Make the second rail the first, which sews first in each pair and starts the column. An S-stitch starts on the second rail instead, and sews every other stitch from it.
anyOf.title: Swap rails

tartan.description: The sett, as Ink/Stitch's tartan editor saves it: an object of JSON whose `palette` gives the stripes, each a colour in brackets and its width in millimetres, such as `(#0000ff)/2.4 (#ffffff)0.4 (#ff0000)/2.4`. A `?` before a width leaves its stripe unsewn, a `*` sews it in the colour of the stripe before it, and a `|` parts the warp's stripes from the weft's. `symmetry` mirrors the sett at its ends rather than repeating it, `scale` scales it in percent, `rotate` turns it in degrees, `offset_x` and `offset_y` move it in millimetres, and stripes no wider than `min_stripe_width` sew as runs. Empty, the fill sews Ink/Stitch's default sett. In VectorCraft, StitchCraft Tartan, a filter, writes the sett from a code of its stripes.
tartan.title: Sett

tartan_angle.description: The angle of the rows to the stripes, in degrees: at -45 they slant across both the warp's and the weft's stripes, as a woven twill's do. At 0 or 90 they run along one direction's stripes. A herringbone's rows run at 45° to the stripes, whatever this angle.
tartan_angle.title: Row angle

ties.description: Where the element gets lock stitches: a few tiny stitches that stop the thread from unravelling where its stitching starts and ends.
ties.title: Lock stitches

trim_after.description: Cut the thread after this element, even if the next one starts close by.
trim_after.title: Trim after

underlay_underpath.description: Travel between the underlay's rows runs inside the fill, under the underlay rows sewn after it. Off, the needle travels along the fill's outline.
underlay_underpath.title: Underlay underpath

underlays_first.description: Sew this element's underlay with the underlays of the elements next to it that set this too and sew in its thread, before any of their top stitches. Where satin columns cross, or a border lies over a fill, every underlay then lies under every top stitch. The underlays sew in the elements' order, then their top stitches in the same order. A trim or a stop after an element ends the elements sewn together, and an element alone sews as it does without this. Ink/Stitch doesn't read it, and sews each element's underlay just before its own top stitches.
underlays_first.title: Underlays first

underpath.description: Travel between rows, or a circular fill's pieces of spiral, runs inside the fill, under those sewn after it, which hide it. Off, the needle travels along the fill's outline, where the travel can show along the edge.
underpath.title: Underpath

zigzag_angle.description: Turns every stitch away from square to the path, in degrees: positive turns clockwise as the drawing shows it. On a curve the turned stitches point like the spokes of a wheel.
zigzag_angle.title: Zigzag angle

anyOf.description: How far it is along the path from one stitch to the next that crosses the same way, a zig and a zag together. Ink/Stitch takes several spacings separated by spaces, and sews the first.
anyOf.title: Zigzag spacing

anyOf.description: The distance from one pair of needle points across the column to the next. A satin column goes across and back in one spacing, an E-stitch sews a spike every spacing, and an S-stitch a stitch across, each the other way from the one before. In a zigzag satin the needle goes across and back in one spacing too, its points on the 2 rails half a spacing apart. It is measured across the column at its outside edge. On a curve the stitches lie closer together at the inside edge.
anyOf.title: Zigzag spacing

anyOf.description: Sew the line as a zigzag across it, the needle going this far along the line from one side to the other and back. 0 sews it as a running stitch.
anyOf.title: Zigzag spacing

zigzag_underlay.description: Sew a sparse zigzag across the column, to its end and back, before the top stitches. It lifts them off the fabric and makes a wide column look fuller.
zigzag_underlay.title: Zigzag underlay

zigzag_underlay_inset_mm.description: How far inside each rail the zigzag's points are. Empty: half the contour's inset, which puts them between the contour and the edge. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
zigzag_underlay_inset_mm.title: Zigzag underlay inset

zigzag_underlay_inset_percent.description: More inset, in percent of the column's width at each point, added to the length above. Empty: half the contour's. 2 values set the first rail's side, then the second's.
zigzag_underlay_inset_percent.title: Zigzag underlay inset (% of width)

zigzag_underlay_max_stitch_length_mm.description: Split zigzag stitches longer than this into equal parts. Empty: none is split.
zigzag_underlay_max_stitch_length_mm.title: Zigzag underlay longest stitch

zigzag_underlay_spacing_mm.description: How far apart the zigzag's points on each rail are, each way.
zigzag_underlay_spacing_mm.title: Zigzag underlay spacing

zigzag_width_mm.description: How wide the zigzag is, from one side of the line to the other.
zigzag_width_mm.title: Zigzag width

title: StitchCraft parameters
